page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highmem-180 is an x86_64 instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors. It is configured with 180 dedicated vCPUs across 90 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system features 1440 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. Local persistent storage is not included, meaning the instance relies on network-attached block storage. The configuration includes no discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core computing capability, recording 277,249.17 on stress-ng multi-core tests and 21,472.0 on Geekbench multi-core evaluation. CPU instruction capabilities include AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, AES, and SHA_NI. Memory throughput measurements show 177.32 GB/s for large uncached write operations and 13,485.99 GB/s for small cached reads. The platform recorded 210.86 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, alongside strong database performance scores in synthetic testing suites.

The absence of integrated local storage shifts input/output operations entirely to attached storage volumes, which represents a key architectural tradeoff for disk-heavy tasks. The high core count and large memory footprint make the c3d-highmem-180 suitable for memory-resident databases, distributed caching tiers, in-memory analytics pipelines, extensive Clang software compilation, and CPU-driven language model inference.
